notes: known_github_hosts is fixed across every case in this file at ["github.com", "ghe.contoso.com"], matching the original test's hosts() helper. PrLinkTarget is a two-variant enum (GitHub{host,owner,repo,number} | Azure{org,project,repo,number}); expected.type names the variant and expected's other fields are its payload. expected: null means parse(...) returns None.

cases.notes: Plain GitHub.com PR link, no trailing tab/query/fragment.

Same PR as github-basic: the /files tab, ?w=1 query and #diff-abc fragment are all discarded by split() before parsing. Proves the trailing path segments after {number} (kind, number, ..) are ignored.

Enterprise host recognized only because it is present in knownGithubHosts. The original test only asserts number==7 via a matches! guard; the full expected shape here is derived directly from parse_github's construction (host is the matched knownGithubHosts entry, not a re-derived string), not an independent assertion in the source test.
Same path shape as github-enterprise-connected-host, but the host is not in knownGithubHosts, so it is indistinguishable from an arbitrary self-hosted git server and parse returns None.
dev.azure.com host; project segment is percent-decoded (%20 -> space) by percent_decode before matching.

Legacy *.visualstudio.com host: org is the subdomain with the suffix stripped. The optional DefaultCollection path segment (matched case-insensitively) is dropped before looking for {project}/_git/{repo}/pullrequest/{n}. The ?_a=files query is discarded by split().

Azure's portal omits the project segment in the URL when the project name matches the repository name; parse_azure's second match arm ([git, repo, pr, number, ..]) fills project with the same value as repo in that case.
Only two path segments; parse_github's [owner, repo, kind, number, ..] destructure has nothing to bind kind/number to.
kind == "issues", which fails the kind.eq_ignore_ascii_case("pull") / "pulls" check.
A plain repo browse link (project/_git/repo, no /pullrequest/{n} tail) matches neither parse_azure match arm.
split() requires a '/' separating host from path (via split_once('/')); a string with none returns None before either provider parser runs.
